findings.reason: an implementer working §6 and one working §7 will each expect to author the same two files (eddb_remote.py, eddb.py), so the plan must name a single section's node as the transport owner and move the design text beside it.
findings.text: the EQDB transport (one request type and one record type in imas_ambix/data/eddb_remote.py, the grid record writer and its two extracted helpers in imas_ambix/data/eddb.py) is designed in §7 but §6 states "§6 builds that transport", while §8's execution order files "the EQDB reader" under §7 and §6's node jtmm-eqdb-reader-probe and §7's open question eqdb-reader both carry "reader" for two different things

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan creates no new module; the EQDB work lands inside the existing eddb_remote.py and eddb.py owners, and the shared token/overwrite contract is deliberately extracted into private helpers so two writers have one implementation rather than a parallel path.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — one shared mechanism, the EQDB transport, is designed in one section and built by another, so ownership of eddb_remote.py's EQDB types and eddb.py's grid writer is split between §6 and §7.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; every section that adds surface names what it retires or why nothing can (§6 adds measure_convention and retires mast_angle_to_canonical; §7 adds the two EQDB public types and retires three PINNED constants plus their re-export; §5's spelling table and §7's two record fields each state why they retire nothing).
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — every mechanism the plan adds cites the existing owner it extends (read_level2_observation, measure_diiid_convention, default_registry, the artifact_resolution pins, eddb_remote/eddb), and each cited symbol was opened and behaves as the plan states (mast_angle_to_canonical's only caller is its own test; project_poloidal_field is live in gs/operator.py; read_level2_observation hard-codes MAST level-2 keys; MAST_TO_COCOS_17_FACTORS is read only by tests; the PINNED-constant reader census is exact: 8/3/9 sites in the three named test modules).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the proposed changes extend existing mechanisms (the transform_engine COCOS step, the description_reader probe_angle_source branch, the machine_identity registry) instead of layering a wrapper over them; no wrapper is added without an extension argument.
